claim: LLM research ideas were rated more novel but slightly less feasible than expert ideas in a blind review, and LLM self-evaluation and diversity of generation failed.
quote: LLM-generated ideas are judged as more novel (p < 0.05) than human expert ideas while being judged slightly weaker on feasibility
title: Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
transfer: Do not trust the model's own novelty ranking. Use an external check (execution, prior-art search) to prune divergent ideas.

claim: After 43 experts executed the ideas, LLM ideas lost their novelty edge: scores fell significantly more than for expert ideas, and humans often ended higher.
quote: the scores of the LLM-generated ideas decrease significantly more than expert-written ideas
title: The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
n: 43 researchers, each executed one idea over 100 hours
transfer: Ideas that look novel on paper are a weak signal. Rank ideas after a cheap execution test, not at the idea stage.

claim: The AI Scientist system gave poor novelty judgements, misclassifying established concepts as new, and 42 percent of its experiments failed from coding errors.
quote: poor novelty assessments, often misclassifying established concepts
title: Evaluating Sakana's AI Scientist: Bold Claims, Mixed Results, and a Promising Future?
transfer: An automatic novelty claim needs a real literature search step and a tested-code step; never self-certify novelty.

claim: A considerable fraction of LLM-generated research documents were found to be smart plagiarism of existing work, and plagiarism detectors missed it.
quote: automated plagiarism detectors are inadequate at catching plagiarized ideas from such systems
title: All That Glitters is Not Novel: Plagiarism in AI Generated Research
transfer: Before calling an idea new, retrieve the closest prior work and ask what differs. Recombination by a model may be recall in disguise.

claim: LLM responses to creativity tests are much more similar to each other than human responses are to each other, so samples from different models add less variety than expected.
quote: LLM responses are much more similar to other LLM responses than human responses are to each other.
title: We're Different, We're the Same: Creative Homogeneity Across LLMs
transfer: Forced divergence must use structural constraints (different frames, forbidden words, distant seeds), not just resampling or switching models.

claim: Writing with a feedback-tuned model (InstructGPT) reduced the diversity of content across writers; the base model did not.
quote: writing with InstructGPT (but not the GPT3) results in a statistically significant reduction in diversity.
title: Does Writing with Language Models Reduce Content Diversity?
transfer: Showing the agent its own earlier ideas can pull later ideas toward the same mode. Generate cards independently, then compare.

claim: Aligned models have lower token entropy and cluster tightly in embedding space, a trade-off between consistency and creativity.
quote: aligned models exhibit lower entropy in token predictions, form distinct clusters in the embedding space
title: Creativity Has Left the Chat: The Price of Debiasing Language Models
transfer: Expect the chat-tuned model to under-explore by default; a diverge step has real headroom on open tasks (matches our NoveltyBench gain).

claim: Professional human authors score about 66 percent higher on a creativity index than LLM text, which borrows more from existing web text.
quote: CREATIVITY INDEX of professional human authors is on average 66.2% higher.
title: AI as Humanity's Salieri: Quantifying Linguistic Creativity of Language Models via Systematic Attribution of Machine Text against Web Text
transfer: Add a check that measures overlap with known text for any claimed novel output.

claim: LLMs do not explore robustly in bandit tasks; only GPT-4 with chain of thought and an externally summarized history explored well.
quote: do not robustly engage in exploration without substantial interventions.
title: Can large language models explore in-context?
n: GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Llama2 across prompt designs
transfer: Exploration should be run by the program (a summarized history of tried options, forced untried branches), not left to the model's in-context judgement.

claim: Without external feedback, self-correction by an LLM struggles and sometimes lowers performance.
quote: LLMs struggle to self-correct their responses without external feedback, and at times, their performance even degrades after self-correction.
authors: Huang, Chen, Mishra, Zheng, Yu, Song, Zhou
title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
transfer: Problem reframing and always-doubt steps need an outside signal (test, example, retrieved fact). Without one, skip the doubt step on single-answer tasks.

claim: AI assistants show sycophancy: responses that match a user's views are more likely to be preferred, so a critic or reframer prompted by the user's idea tends to agree.
quote: sycophancy is a general behavior of state-of-the-art AI assistants.
title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
transfer: Run the critic blind to which idea is the favorite; ask it to rank, not to approve.

claim: The reported decline in the disruption index of papers and patents is partly an artefact of database entries with zero references.
quote: their source documents predominantly do make references, exposing them as pure dataset artefacts.
title: Dataset Artefacts are the Hidden Drivers of the Declining Disruptiveness in Science
n: reanalysis of the Park et al. data
transfer: Do not use disruption or citation-style scores as an agent's signal for what is a breakthrough; the measures are fragile.

claim: A literature review finds disruption indices suffer from inconsistency, time-sensitive biases and data-induced biases; variants differ in validity.
quote: disruption indices suffer from inconsistency, time-sensitive biases, and several data-induced biases.
title: What do we know about the disruption index in scientometrics? An overview of the literature
transfer: Same as above: no clean machine-readable score for breakthrough exists; use task-specific external checks.

claim: Atypical combinations of cited journals predicted high-impact papers only when paired with a conventional core, in about 18 million papers; this is the base claim that later critiques test.
title: Atypical Combinations and Scientific Impact
transfer: Mix mostly conventional framing with one distant element, rather than going fully distant. Page returned 403 so numbers need re-checking.

claim: Highly novel papers are cited late and are riskier and slower to be recognised, so early signals understate them.
title: Bias against novelty in science: A cautionary tale for users of bibliometric indicators
transfer: Do not drop an idea only because early checks score it low; keep a small reserve of high-novelty candidates for a longer test. Not opened.

claim: Recombining distant elements raises the variance of outcomes: mean usefulness falls while the chance of both big success and failure rise.
title: Recombinant Uncertainty in Technological Search
transfer: Distant recombination needs many cheap tries plus a fast filter; one distant try is mostly a loss. Not opened.

claim: People reject creative ideas when they feel uncertainty, even when they say they want creativity. This applies to human raters and may apply to LLM judges.
title: The Bias Against Creativity: Why People Desire but Reject Creative Ideas
transfer: Evaluator prompts should rate novelty and usefulness on separate scales so uncertainty does not suppress the novel idea. Not opened.

claim: Face-to-face brainstorming groups produce fewer ideas than the same people working alone and pooled. Applies to teams only.
title: Productivity loss in brainstorming groups: A meta-analytic integration
transfer: Team-only finding, but it supports generating independently then pooling, which one agent can do with isolated calls. Not opened.

claim: Generating ideas individually first, then sharing and selecting, produced a better best idea than team brainstorming. Applies to teams.
title: Idea Generation and the Quality of the Best Idea
transfer: Matches our design: independent diverge calls, then a separate selection step. Not opened.

claim: Generative AI help raised individual story creativity but made stories more alike across writers, a collective diversity cost.
title: Generative AI enhances individual creativity but reduces the collective diversity of novel content
transfer: One agent run many times will look good per run and similar across runs; measure distinctness across runs, as NoveltyBench does. Page returned 403.
